sections.content: How many people stayed in York after gaining qualifications?

York is a large town in Yorkshire and The Humber. York also has a university.

York has lower levels of deprivation.

Overall, York ended up with:

  • more graduates than it produced
  • more non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 5,220 state-school pupils from York who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 1,640 (31%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 1,645 (32%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare York to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of York's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in York in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left York move to?

Of York's graduates, 600 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 70 of those graduates (12%) were living fairly locally, in the York travel to work area (TTWA).

Of York's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 350 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 125 of those qualified non-graduates (36%) were living fairly locally, in the York travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in York's GCSE cohort:

  • 430 graduates left Yorkshire and The Humber
  • the most common region they moved to was London
  • 135 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left Yorkshire and The Humber
  • the most common region they moved to was London

In 2018 to 2019, 70% of graduates and 37% of qualified non-graduates living in York had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 3,335 graduates and 1,990 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in York. This is compared with the 1,640 graduates and 1,645 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 30% of the graduates had also lived in York as GCSE pupils, while 70% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in York in 2018 to 2019, 63% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 37% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
